paraphrase: Self and dharmas are refuted: they are mere designations based on the transformations of consciousness; the self of the non-Buddhists and the real dharmas of the Hīnayāna schools are both rejected.
notes: Fascicle (juan)-level reference, from memory; to be checked against T1585.

paraphrase: At buddhahood the eight consciousnesses are transformed into four wisdoms: the eighth into great mirror-wisdom, the seventh into equality-wisdom, the sixth into discerning wisdom, the five senses into the wisdom that accomplishes what is to be done; the sixth and seventh begin to turn at the path of seeing, the eighth and the five senses only at buddhahood.
notes: Fascicle (juan)-level reference, from memory; to be checked against T1585.

paraphrase: Every cognition has four parts: the seen part (image), the seeing part, the self-witnessing part and the witnessing of the self-witnessing part (Dharmapāla's view, against those who admit one, two or three parts); seeds are both originally present and newly perfumed.
notes: Fascicle (juan)-level reference, from memory; to be checked against T1585.

paraphrase: The path to cognition-only has five stages: accumulation, preparation (with the four stages heat, peak, patience and supreme mundane quality, in which the grasped and then the grasper are seen as empty), penetration (the path of seeing), cultivation (through the ten grounds), and final attainment.
notes: Fascicle (juan)-level reference, from memory; to be checked against T1585. The five-stage account spans juan 9–10.
